To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the critical pressure for the magnetic /structural transition is larger in EuFe2As 2 with a higher residual resistivity ratio.

(a) the magnetic/structural transition is induced by the pressure and the superconducting phase emerges at the critical pressure; (b) the critical pressure for the samples with higher residual resistivity ratio is slightly higher than that for the samples with lower residual resistivity ratio; (c) the superconducting transition is not affected by the pressure, and the critical temperature is almost unchanged.

the critical pressure for the suppression of the antiferromagnetic transition in the FeAs layers of EuFe2 As2 is slightly but distinctively larger than the critical pressure for superconductivity in this compound.

a systematic investigation of the effect of pressure on the superconducting and magnetic properties of the Fe-based superconductors.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the pressure-induced superconductivity is a robust phenomenon in EuFe2As 2 single crystals, but the pressure for the superconducting transition is dependent on the residual resistivity ratio of samples.

high-pressure resistivity measurements of EuFe2AS2 single crystals with different RRRs are consistent with the scenario that the magnetic/structural transition in this compound is driven by the FeAs layers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the critical pressure is independent on the residual resistivity ratio, and that the critical pressure of 2.7 Gpa is consistent with the pressure for the disappearance of the antiferromagnetic order in EuFe2As.

the magnetic/structural transition temperature T0 in the samples with RRC = 7 and 7 is 194K and 190K, respectively, and the critical pressure for the disappearance of the magnetic/structural transitions in the samples with 7 and 5 is 2.5GPa and 2.7GPa, respectively.
the critical pressure is determined by the RRR value, and that the superconducting transition is suppressed with increasing pressure for samples with R = 7, 10, 12 and 15.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given material, the critical pressure, where the magnetic /structural transition is suppressed to zero, is not sensitive to the sample quality.

the superconductivity in EuFe2As 2 single crystals with RRR =7 is induced by the application of a pressure of 2.5 Gpa, whereas for the samples with a RRR = 15, a pressure of 3.0GPa is necessary to induce superconductivity.
the superconductivity in EuFe2As 2 single crystals is induced by the application of hydrostatic pressure and the superconductivity is suppressed by the magnetic ordering.
